correctness.rationale: Let P_b denote positive base-b palindromes and D_b all positive differences of two of them. For each integer b>=5, T=b^3-(b-1)^2, whose base-b digits are ((b-1),1,(b-1)). Two- and three-digit palindrome families J_a=a(b+1), P_{a,c}=a(b^2+1)+cb yield consecutive intervals [W-(b-1),W-1] of differences from one-digit palindromes; between gaps are filled by exact identities J_a=J_(a+1)-J_1, J_a+1=(111)_b-J_(b-a), P_{a,c}=P_(b-1,c)-P_(b-1-a,0), P_{a,b-1}+1=(1111)_b-P_(b-a,1), and P_(b-1,0)=(1111)_b-P_(2,0). Therefore all 1<=d<T are differences. To rule out T, the quantitative large-palindrome reduction in the PROOF of Pongsriiam–Saito Theorem 12 implies smaller palindrome u<b^5 for this three-digit difference; v=u+T then has at most six base-b digits. Within equal lengths the leading/trailing-digit difference cannot be b-1 mod b; unequal lengths 3/2,4/<=3,5/4,6/5 are excluded by leading digits, modulus and two coefficient identities. Independent finite checks construct differences for every d<T in bases 5..12 and test all positive palindromes u<b^5 for forbidden T, none found. The symbolic case analysis plus the cited reduction, not the finite search, establishes every b>=5.
residual_risks: The universal nonrepresentation relies on the precise quantitative bound extracted from the proof of Theorem 12, not merely on its published infinitude statement.
The claim excludes bases 2,3,4 and makes no assertion about later gaps, full difference sets or their densities.

value.rationale: Uniformly identifies the first omitted element of a natural base-dependent arithmetic difference set for every b>=5. It extends base-by-base observations into a complete family theorem, requiring nontrivial interplay of explicit coverage and long-palindrome rigidity, a useful exact invariant independently of full difference-set classification.
residual_risks: Only the least missing gap is obtained; no density or complete characterization of palindrome differences follows.
